note: This first stage executes ayaana/baana only after an overt preceding clause boundary. A standalone connective form is left unjudged rather than assumed to have omitted context.

rule: For reviewed common-noun true subject focus in the second clause, ayaana/baana inherits the same absolute/non-subject case requirement as base ayaa/baa.
After removing only connective -na, predicate agreement is delegated unchanged to the reviewed restrictive subject-focus analyzer for base ayaa/baa.
ayaana/baana in this stage are not negative-focus markers and are not generalized to subject-clitic+connective forms. ayaan remains the distinct negative-focus spelling already modeled elsewhere.
